F6.quote: I’m delighted that after more than four years of work by Lillian-Yvonne Bertram and myself — we’re co-editors of this book — the MIT Press and Counterpath have jointly published
F6.claim: the co-editor: after more than four years of work, Bertram and Montfort co-edited the book, published jointly by the MIT Press and Counterpath

F7.claim: the announcement was posted 2024-11-05 (updated 2025-04-01, the two dates run together on the page)

F8.quote: This anthology spans seven decades of computer-generated text, beginning before the term “artificial intelligence” was even coined.
F8.claim: the anthology spans seven decades of computer-generated text, beginning before the term 'artificial intelligence' was coined
F8.lineage: the argument against a recent origin of text generation

F9.quote: While not restricted to poetry, fiction, and other creative projects, it reveals the rich work that has been done by artists, poets, and other sorts of writers who have taken computing and code into their own hands.
F9.claim: not restricted to creative projects, it shows the work of artists, poets and other writers who took computing and code into their own hands

F10.quote: The anthology includes examples of powerful and principled rhetorical generation along with story generation systems based on cognitive research. There are examples of “real news” generation that has already been informing us — along with hoaxes and humor.
F10.claim: it includes rhetorical generation, story generation systems based on cognitive research, 'real news' generation, hoaxes and humor

F11.quote: It’s all contextualized by brief introductions to each excerpt, longer introductions to each fine-grained genre of text generation, and an overall introduction that Lillian-Yvonne and I wrote.
F11.claim: introductions to each excerpt, longer introductions to each fine-grained genre of text generation, and an overall introduction by the two editors

F12.quote: There are 200 selections in the 500-page book, which we hope will be a valuable sourcebook for academics and students — but also a way for general readers to learn about innovations in computing and writing.
F12.claim: 200 selections in the 500-page book, hoped to be a sourcebook for academics and students and a way for general readers to learn about innovations in computing and writing

F13.quote: Book launch events are posted here and will be updated as new ones are scheduled!
F13.claim: the post lists the book's launches, talks and events (November 2024 to April 2025, as listed)
F13.lineage: reception: launches and the recorded launch

F14.claim: the European launch at the University of Bergen's Center for Digital Narrative, with the editors, Scott Rettberg and Tegan Pyke, was streamed and recorded for YouTube
F14.lineage: reception: launches and the recorded launch

F18.quote: Output: An Anthology of Computer-Generated Text, 1953–2023 , edited by Lillian Yvonne-Bertram and Nick Montfort
F18.claim: the publisher's title line, printing the first editor as 'Lillian Yvonne-Bertram'

F19.quote: An anthology of seven decades of English-language outputs from computer generation systems, chronicling the vast history of machine-written texts created long before ChatGPT.
F19.claim: an anthology of seven decades of English-language outputs from computer generation systems, chronicling the history of machine-written texts made long before ChatGPT
F19.lineage: what it is: seven decades of output from generation systems

F20.quote: The discussion of computer-generated text has recently reached a fever pitch, but largely omits the long history of work in this area—text generation, as it happens, was not invented yesterday in Silicon Valley.
F20.claim: the discussion of computer-generated text omits its long history; text generation was not invented yesterday in Silicon Valley
F20.lineage: the argument against a recent origin of text generation

F21.quote: This anthology, Output , thoughtfully selected, introduced, and edited by Lillian-Yvonne Bertram and Nick Montfort, aims to correct that omission by gathering seven decades of English-language texts produced by generation systems and software.
F21.claim: selected, introduced and edited by Bertram and Montfort, it aims to correct that omission by gathering seven decades of English-language texts produced by generation systems and software
F21.lineage: what it is: seven decades of output from generation systems

F22.quote: The outputs span many different types of creative writing and include text generated by research systems, along with reports and utilitarian texts, representing many general advances and experiments in text generation.
F22.claim: the outputs span many types of creative writing and include research-system text, reports and utilitarian texts

F23.quote: Output is first and foremost a collection of outputs to be encountered by readers.
F23.claim: first and foremost a collection of outputs to be encountered by readers
F23.lineage: readership: a collection to be read

F24.quote: In addition to an overall introduction, each of the excerpts is introduced individually and organized by fine-grain genre including conversations, humor, letters, poetry, prose, and sentences.
F24.claim: an overall introduction; each excerpt introduced individually and organized by fine-grain genre (conversations, humor, letters, poetry, prose, sentences)

F25.quote: Bibliographic references allow readers to learn more about outputs and systems that intrigue them.
F25.claim: bibliographic references lead readers to outputs and systems

F26.quote: Although Output could serve as a reference book, it is designed to be readable and to be read.
F26.claim: it could serve as a reference book and is designed to be readable and read
F26.lineage: readership: a collection to be read

F27.quote: Purposefully excluded are human–computer collaborations that were conceptually defined but not implemented as a computer system.
F27.claim: the admission rule: human–computer collaborations conceptually defined but not implemented as a computer system are excluded

F28.quote: Lillian-Yvonne Bertram is the author of Travesty Generator , a book of computational poetry that was longlisted for the 2020 National Book Award for Poetry, and several other poetry books. They direct the MFA in Creative Writing program at the University of Maryland.
F28.claim: Bertram, author of Travesty Generator (computational poetry, longlisted for the 2020 National Book Award for Poetry), directs the MFA in Creative Writing at the University of Maryland
F28.lineage: the editors and their computer-generated books

F29.quote: Nick Montfort is a poet and artist who uses computation as his medium. He is the series editor of Counterpath’s Using Electricity series, and author of The Truelist and #! , both from Counterpath.
F29.claim: Montfort, a poet and artist who uses computation as his medium, edits Counterpath's Using Electricity series and wrote The Truelist and #!
F29.lineage: the editors and their computer-generated books

F30.quote: He is Professor of Digital Media at MIT and Principal Investigator in the Center for Digital Narrative at the University of Bergen, Norway.
F30.claim: Montfort is Professor of Digital Media at MIT and Principal Investigator in the Center for Digital Narrative, University of Bergen
F30.lineage: the editors and their computer-generated books
